claims.text: Adding a trace concentration of yttrium to CoCrFeNi will promote in situ formation of a Y-containing oxide scale during sliding.
The Y-containing oxide scale will be stable, adherent, and lubricious.
The Y-containing oxide scale will maintain low friction and wear from room temperature through 800 °C.
Yttrium will produce a finely structured oxide scale.
Yttrium will enhance oxide-scale adhesion and morphology at elevated temperatures.
Improved scale adhesion and morphology will minimize oxide spallation.
Reduced oxide spallation will enable development of a continuous lubricious boundary film.
Yttrium addition will preserve low friction at lower temperatures.
Y-doped CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than undoped CoCrFeNi over the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C regime.
Y-doped CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than undoped CoCrFeNi over the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C regime.
Undoped CoCrFeNi has variable tribological performance because of uncontrolled oxidation across the temperature range.
Undoped CoCrFeNi has variable tribological performance because of phase instability across the temperature range.
The proposed effect is expected under sliding in an oxidizing atmosphere from room temperature to 800 °C.
The performance benefit may depend on the exact test conditions.
